designation: IN THE COURT OF DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE
jurisdictionNote: District-level criminal and civil courts in Haryana, governed by the Punjab Courts Act, 1918 (as in force in Haryana) read with the Punjab and Haryana High Court Rules and Orders (Volumes I-VI). Sessions courts try offences punishable with imprisonment exceeding 7 years. Haryana presently comprises 22 revenue districts and the subordinate judiciary is supervised by the Punjab and Haryana High Court at Chandigarh, which is the common High Court for the States of Punjab and Haryana and the Union Territory of Chandigarh. Hindi is the official language of the State subordinate courts under the Haryana Official Language Act, 1969.

party_designation.state: State of Haryana through the Principal Secretary, Home Department, Government of Haryana, Chandigarh

prayer_language.opening: It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court may graciously be pleased to:
prayer_language.closing: And for this act of kindness, the petitioner shall, as in duty bound, ever pray.

verification_format:
I, {deponent_name}, {designation}, do hereby solemnly verify and declare that the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ of the above petition are true to my personal knowledge and the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ are based on information received and legal advice tendered, which I believe to be true. Nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

DEPONENT
localRules: Hindi is the official language of the Haryana subordinate courts under the Haryana Official Language Act, 1969; pleadings before the Punjab and Haryana High Court are in English. District court pleadings may be filed in English with Hindi translation where required.
Bail applications under S.483 BNSS (formerly S.439 CrPC) before the Sessions Court must disclose any prior rejection by a Magistrate or co-ordinate court.
Anticipatory bail applications (S.482 BNSS) must be accompanied by an affidavit, certified copy of the FIR and grounds of apprehension.
Vakalatnama in the form prescribed under the Punjab and Haryana High Court Rules and Orders, Volume V (as adopted by Haryana) to be filed at the first instance with requisite court-fee stamp.
All civil pleadings to be paginated, indexed and accompanied by a list of documents under Order VII / Order VIII CPC.
Court-fee under the Court-Fees Act, 1870 as in force in Haryana with State amendments; ad valorem fee structure applies to civil suits.
Atrocities (SC/ST), POCSO and NDPS cases are tried by designated Special Courts notified by the State Government — typically the District & Sessions Judge at the district headquarters.
Designated Special Courts also exist for offences under the Haryana Prohibition of Ragging Act, 2012 and the Haryana Protection of Witnesses Act provisions where notified.
Gurugram (Gurgaon) and Faridabad host the largest district court establishments in the National Capital Region; Panchkula hosts the headquarters complex adjacent to the High Court.
e_filing_note: e-Filing is operational at Gurugram, Faridabad, Panchkula and Rohtak via the eCourts portal; not yet mandatory state-wide.
